narration.transcript: Want the look of old timber beams without the weight? Meet Heritage Timber by Ekena Millwork. Each beam is cast from real, weathered timber, so it looks solid, even up close. A five and a half inch beam, 12 feet long, ships at about 18 pounds. One person can lift it. It slides over a wood block with standard household tools, and it's hollow so it can hide wiring. And unlike solid wood, it resists warping and cracking with less upkeep. And here it is in real customers' homes. Pick from six hand-stained finishes or primed, eight cross-section sizes in lengths from four to 24 feet. It's in stock and usually ships in three to five business days. Order a sample and see it in your own light.

findings.rule: HOUSE_RULES.md rule 6: the edit is timed to the music's beats
findings.what: The finish changes are now two beats apart, but every one lands late. Measured centres of the beam cross-fade (16:9; the 9:16 label swaps match): f2421.9, 2479.3, 2537.2, 2595.9, 2652.9, 2711.3, against beats at 2411.7, 2468.8, 2527.4, 2584.5, 2643.0, 2700.1. That is +10 to +11 frames (165-190 ms) every time. On the strip, Sandstone is still fully on screen at f2416 and Kona Brown only takes over around f2424. The first label (Sandstone) also fades in centred on about f2369, between beats 2354.6 and 2382.5. The manifest says the dissolves are centred on the beat; in 'choose' they are not (in 'homes' they are).
findings.fix: render/videos/heritage-hero.mjs, 'choose' finish cycle: centre each cross-fade (label out/in and beam dissolve) on the beat instead of starting it about on the beat, i.e. move the whole cycle about 10 frames (0.17 s) earlier so the swaps centre on f2411.7, 2468.8, 2527.4, 2584.5, 2643.0, 2700.1. Do the same for the first label's fade-in (centre it on 2354.6 or 2382.5). Use the same centring code the 'homes' montage uses, since that one measures on the beat.
